answer: Non-transferable receipt chaining resists Sybil attacks: every completed job mints a receipt bound to the worker key, stamped with time and counterparty, and receipts cannot be sold or copied - an echo of real work, not a tradable token. Influence is the sum of receipts, weighted by how recent and how diverse the counterparties are. A relic of old work fades, so a fake cannot buy history; it must earn it. Like saffron, genuine receipts are costly to produce in bulk: each one needs a real client, real payment, and real time, so a thousand fakes need a thousand genuine transactions.
